AgentCreate.description:
The body of `POST /agents`: an agent of your team or of your own.

The agent declares what it IS (instructions, an optional plugin agent, MCP servers, limits, the
credentials it needs). The PLATFORM decides what it runs on: the image, the model and the harness
are your tenant's free-prompt runtime, and the network it reaches never goes beyond your tenant's
policy. An agent needs at least `instructions` or a `plugin_agent`.

credentials.description: Names of the credentials the agent may be given as `workspace.credentials_ref` (what `capabilities.credentials` lists in `GET /agents`). Plain names only; the agent's MCP servers do not need to be listed here.

denied_tools.description: Tools every task of this agent is DENIED, as Claude Code permission rules: `Tool`, `Tool(specifier)`, `mcp__<server>`, `mcp__<server>__<tool>` or `mcp__<server>__*` (up to 64 rules of up to 512 characters). Joined to the ones your tenant's policy denies, which an agent cannot take away. Omit it to deny nothing beyond the policy. A malformed rule is `422 denied_tools_invalid`.
denied_tools.title: Denied Tools

description.description: What the agent is for, shown in `GET /agents`.

egress.description: Narrows the network the agent reaches. Omit it to inherit everything your tenant's policy grants a free prompt; send it to keep only these destinations (plus the model gateway and the object store the run needs). A destination beyond the policy is `422 agent_egress_not_allowed`: it can never widen it.
egress.title: Egress

env_credentials.description: Credentials the agent receives as ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES of its container: `{VARIABLE: credential}`. `VARIABLE` is `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$` and not one the runtime uses (`ANTHROPIC_*`, `AGENT_*`, `MCP_*`, `CLAUDE_*`, `PATH`, `HOME`, ... : `422 env_var_invalid`). A `team` agent names credentials of the team as `shared:<name>` (`GET /credentials?scope=shared`); a `personal` agent names its owner's own. A credential that does not exist, or that the agent cannot use, is `422 credential_unavailable` or `422 shared_credential_not_allowed`. The value never appears in the task, the API or the published logs, but the agent can print it: use credentials with the least permission that does the job.

image.description: Image the agent runs on instead of the platform's: `repository:tag` or `repository@sha256:...`, from a PUBLIC registry (Docker Hub when no registry is named). The farm resolves the tag to its digest and reads those labels when it accepts each task (`422 image_not_found`, `422 registry_auth_required`, `422 image_labels_invalid`, `503 registry_unavailable`). A task can send its own.

McpServerIn.description:
A remote MCP server (HTTP) the agent can use during this task. The secret never travels in the
task: it is one of YOUR credentials, named here.

Two forms, told apart by whether `url` is present:

- **The credential is the address** (no `url`): for servers whose URL carries the key in its path,
  such as `https://portal.example.com/mcp/<key>`. Register the whole URL as a credential of type
  `mcp_url`. The URL is then never in the task, the API, the logs or the result.
- **A public address and a token** (`url` present): register the token as a credential of type
  `mcp_token`. It is sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`, or as the header named in `header`.

**Servers of the house.** The deployment can offer some by name (see the deployment's documentation). With no
`url` and one of those names, the server is the house's: its address and header are fixed, the
credential is an `mcp_token` and `header` must be omitted. Those names are reserved: an `mcp_url`
credential under one of them is refused (`422 mcp_credential_type_mismatch`).

A team agent (`POST /agents`, `scope: team`) names a credential of the team as `shared:<name>` (`GET /credentials?scope=shared`), and has to when it sends a `url`.

header.description: Only with `url`. Header that carries the token. Default `Authorization`, sent as `Bearer <token>`; any other header carries the token as is.

name.title: Name

NotifyTargetIn.description:
A destination the farm notifies about this task: when it ends (`final`) and each time its agent
sends a message (`message`). The farm sends it itself, with retries; the agent never sees the URL.

What the destination receives depends on `format`:

- **`teams`**: a message with an Adaptive Card, for a Teams workflow ("When a Teams webhook request
  is received") or any endpoint that takes one;
- **`slack`**: a Slack message (`text` and `blocks`), for an incoming webhook;
- **`json`**: the farm's own envelope, signed with the farm's Ed25519 key
  (`X-Agent-Farm-Signature-Ed25519` over `"<X-Agent-Farm-Timestamp>.<raw body>"`, key named by
  `X-Agent-Farm-Key-Id` among those of `GET /notify-key`), for an application of yours.

The URL is a secret of yours: it is never returned by the API (`GET /tasks/{task_id}` shows only
`format` and `events`), never written to a log, never shown to the agent, and it is deleted once the
task's final notifications have been delivered or given up. The other kind of destination is
`conversation`: the chat a task came from, which the farm answers in itself (the chat channel sets it;
the public API refuses it). `GET /tasks/{task_id}` shows only its `kind` and `events`.

events.description: What this destination is told: `final` (the task ended: its state, duration, last progress and a short summary) and/or `message` (what the task's agent sends while it works). Default: both.
events.title: Events

format.description: Required with `kind: url`. What the body is: `teams` (Adaptive Card), `slack` (`text` + `blocks`) or `json` (the farm's signed envelope; `422 notify_not_enabled` on a deployment that does not sign).
format.title: Format

kind.description: `url` (default): the farm posts to your `url`. `conversation`: the chat the task came from; only a chat channel sets it on the tasks it starts, the public API answers `422 notify_kind_not_allowed`. A `conversation` has no `url` nor `format`.
kind.title: Kind

url.description: Required with `kind: url`. `https` URL on port 443, without credentials in its authority, whose host resolves to public internet addresses only (`422 notify_url_invalid` / `422 notify_destination_refused`). Any public address is accepted. Checked when the task is created and again before every request.
url.title: Url

NotifyTargetIn.title: NotifyTargetIn

info.description:
Control plane of the agent farm: run an AI agent on a task, follow it, read its result and logs,
and schedule it to repeat. Everything here is scoped to the tenant and, within it, to the person
whose key is used. A key with `farm:platform:read` can read any tenant by adding `?tenant=<slug>` to a
`GET`; nothing else ever acts outside the key's own tenant.

**How to use it.** Authenticate every call with `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Start with
`GET /whoami` (who you are, whether you are a tenant admin, when the key expires) and
`GET /agents` (what you can launch and what each agent needs). Launch with `POST /tasks`, poll
`GET /tasks/{task_id}` until `state` is terminal, then `GET /tasks/{task_id}/result`.

**Errors** always have the shape `{"error": {"code", "message", "retryable", "details"}}`; branch on `code`, and repeat only when
`retryable` is true.
Each operation lists the codes it can return. Someone else's resource is `404`, never `403`.

**Cost and safety.** Running a task spends model tokens and tenant capacity. What you put in a
`prompt` or `input` is stored by the farm and can reach logs: never put secrets in it, register
them with `POST /credentials` and refer to them by name.
info.title: Agent Farm — Farm API

get.description:
The agent catalogue for your tenant. For each agent: its `slug` (the `agent_id` to send to `POST /tasks`), its `scope` (`platform`, `team` or `personal`), what it does, whether it `requires_workspace`, which credential names and network destinations it may use (`capabilities`) and its default limits. Read this before building a task so the request is not rejected. Read-only, free.

When a task names an agent, the farm looks for your own personal one first, then your team's, then the platform's. Creating an agent refuses a slug the platform or your team already uses, so a personal agent can never take the place of a platform one.

**Needs scope:** `farm:tasks:read`.

post.description:
Defines an agent you launch by its `slug` (`agent_id` in `POST /tasks`). It declares its `instructions` (they travel in front of the task's `input`: the agent reads them as the start of its task, not as a system prompt), an optional `plugin_agent`, its `mcp_servers`, default `limits` and the `credentials` it may be given. It can run on its own `image` (a public one that carries the farm's layer), with `services` next to it in its pod and a larger `/work` (`work_size`); the model and the harness are your tenant's free-prompt runtime, and its network never goes beyond your tenant's policy: `egress` can only narrow it.

`scope: team` is usable by everybody in the tenant and only a tenant admin (`farm:tenant:admin`) can create it (`403 insufficient_scope` otherwise); `scope: personal` is yours alone. The slug cannot be one a platform agent or one of your team's already has (`409 agent_slug_taken`), so what you launch by name is never ambiguous.

A team agent's MCP servers and credentials are those of whoever launches it; a personal agent's are its owner's. **State change:** stores the definition; nothing runs and nothing is spent.

**Needs scope:** `farm:tasks:write`.

post.description:
Offboards a person (or an integration's key) of your tenant in one call, by `person_id`.

**Dry run by default:** with no body, or `dry_run: true`, nothing changes. The answer lists by name and count what an offboarding would remove and hand over, and any warning (an invalid `transfer_to`, a recipient that is an integration's key, a `service` person, a channel's list of e-mails).

**State change** (`dry_run: false`), in this order: the person is marked offboarded (their keys get `403 person_offboarded`, their chat answers that they have no access, their schedules do not fire); their unfinished tasks are cancelled; their schedules are deleted; their personal agents are deleted; the team agents and shared credentials they created pass to `transfer_to` (or to you); their chat links end and their unused link codes and upload tickets are deleted; their personal credentials are deleted, value and record. Finished tasks stay until retention removes them. It cannot be undone: `POST /people/{person_id}/readmit` lets the person in again but brings nothing back.

**Idempotent:** repeating it finds nothing left and answers `200` with every count at `0`. If the cluster or the secret store does not answer it stops with `503` and `details.done` (what it had already done, which stays done); repeat the same request to finish.

Only an admin of the tenant (`farm:tenant:admin`), for a person of their own tenant: another tenant's `person_id` is `404`. You cannot offboard yourself.

**Needs scope:** `farm:tenant:admin`, `farm:tasks:write`, `farm:tasks:cancel`, `farm:credentials:write`.

post.description:
Runs the same task again and again on a cron expression, without anyone re-sending the request. `task` is exactly a `POST /tasks` body and is validated now, with the same errors, so a schedule that could never run is refused up front; it is validated again on every firing.

Without `recurrence` the schedule never fires on its own: it is a saved task that runs only with `POST /schedules/{schedule_id}/fire`. `name` (for people, not unique) and `metadata` (a free object returned as sent and never passed to the tasks) are optional.

**Cost:** each firing is a real task that spends model tokens, so a frequent cron adds up. Count the firings before creating one. The tenant has a cap on schedules with a recurrence (`429 quota_exceeded`); one without a recurrence does not count.

**Behaviour:** the cron is evaluated in `recurrence.timezone` (08:00 stays 08:00 across DST). If the farm was down, at most ONE catch-up firing happens and the rest are counted in `missed_runs`. A firing never depends on your key still being valid. A fired task belongs to the schedule's owner and has `origin: schedule`.

**State change:** creates the schedule `active` (or `finished` if its first occurrence is already past `ends_at`).

**Needs scope:** `farm:tasks:write`.

post.description:
Runs the schedule's task right now, as a firing outside its cron: the task belongs to the schedule's owner, has `origin: schedule` and shows up in `GET /schedules/{schedule_id}/tasks`. The schedule's next occurrence, `missed_runs` and `runs_count` do not change. The task body is validated again, so a body that stopped validating answers its `422`.

**Cost:** a real task that spends model tokens.

**State change:** creates one task. A `paused` or `finished` schedule answers `409 schedule_not_active`; with `overlap: skip` and a task still running, `409 schedule_overlap`; when its owner has been offboarded from the tenant, `409 schedule_owner_offboarded`, no task, and the schedule is paused.

**Needs scope:** `farm:tasks:write`.

get.description:
Lists your tasks (a tenant admin sees everyone's; add `owner=me` to see only their own). Newest first (unless `updated_since`, below), in pages: when `next_cursor` is not null, pass it as `cursor` for the next page. **Following changes:** pass `updated_since`. The order is then oldest change first, by `updated_at` (ties by task), and `next_cursor` continues in that order; follow it until it is null. A task that changes while you page comes out again later in the same round, with its new `updated_at`. For the next round ask for `updated_since = <greatest updated_at seen> - 30 s` (a write stamped just before that instant can become visible a little later) and drop what you already have by `(task_id, updated_at)`. A cursor from one kind of listing is a `422` in the other.

Read-only, free. Each item is the full task, except that `queue_position` is only on `GET /tasks/{task_id}`. For a tenant admin each task also carries `owner`.

With `tenant=*`: the tasks of every tenant your key can see, in the same order and pages, with the same filters and cursor; each task carries its `tenant`.

**Needs scope:** `farm:tasks:read`.

post.description:
Starts a new task. Send exactly one of `agent_id` (a catalogue agent, see `GET /agents`, plus its `input`) or `prompt` (free-form, only for tenants that allow it).

**Cost:** every task runs a model and consumes tenant capacity and model spend; it is not free to try out. Check `GET /agents` for what an agent needs (a `workspace`, a credential) before sending.

**State change:** creates the task in `pending`; the farm then queues and runs it. Nothing is returned about the outcome: poll `GET /tasks/{task_id}`, then fetch `GET /tasks/{task_id}/result` once the state is terminal.

**Idempotent:** the same `correlation_id` from the same person never creates a second task: the answer is `200` with the existing one (and, if it could not be dispatched the first time, the dispatch is retried). Use a new `correlation_id` for a genuinely new task.

**Notifications:** with `notify`, the farm tells up to five public `https` addresses of yours (a Teams workflow, a Slack webhook, an application) when the task ends and each time its agent sends a message, in the `format` each one takes; see `NotifyTargetIn`. The URLs are never returned.

**Never put secrets in `prompt` or `input`:** they are stored and can reach logs. Register secrets with `POST /credentials` and refer to them by name.

The `tenant` is never accepted in the body (`tenant_not_accepted`): it comes from your key.

**Needs scope:** `farm:tasks:write`.

get.description:
The full task: its state, failure reason, limits, timings and usage so far. After `POST /tasks`, ask until `state` is `succeeded`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `expired`. While `queued`, `queue_position` says how many tasks are ahead.

Add `wait=<seconds>` (0 to 30) to make the call do the waiting: it answers as soon as the task is in a terminal state, or when the seconds run out with whatever state it has then. Above 30 is a `422`, never a shorter wait. Chain calls for longer waits.

A task launched with `notify` carries `notify`: the `format` and `events` of each destination, never its URL.

Read-only, free. A task that is not yours answers `404`, the same as one that does not exist.

**Needs scope:** `farm:tasks:read`.

A conversation larger than 32 MiB is not read: `413 transcript_too_large`. Read-only and free; recorded in the audit trail. It holds what the agent read and wrote, so treat it as sensitive.
